verdict_reason: The Two-NN estimator itself is faithful to Facco et al. 2017: against the RELEASED scikit-dimension 0.3.4 TwoNN on uniform d-cubes at N=2000 it reads 2.0488 / 2.9656 / 4.4993 / 6.9421 versus skdim's 2.0455 / 2.9607 / 4.4919 / 6.9308 for d = 2 / 3 / 5 / 8 (within 0.16% at every d), analytic Pareto(1,d) draws return 2.000808 / 5.047216 / 8.045247 / 20.525964 for d = 2 / 5 / 8 / 20, and its invariances are exact (zero-padding d=768 -> 4096 bit-identical at 9.853618665; a 5-manifold in ambient d = 5..768 gives 4.3771 throughout). YELLOW, not GREEN, for ONE concrete value-changing counterexample: the sklearn CPU fallback is float32 + the x^2+y^2-2xy Gram identity, exactly the form the GPU branch's own comment says inflates TwoNN by up to +23%, and on an 83x768 float32 cloud carrying duplicate rows it returns 9.349137858 against a float64 truth of 9.853619720 (-5.1198%), with 81/83 rows disagreeing on r1. The same estimate is therefore host-dependent.
comparable_reason: Width-invariant EXACTLY -- zero-padding d=768 -> 4096 changes nothing (rel 0.000e+00) and ambient embedding of a fixed 5-manifold gives 4.3771 at every ambient dimension -- so this is NOT a d_model proxy. It IS strongly sample-size dependent: a uniform 8-cube reads 6.7136 / 6.9569 / 7.5629 / 7.2975 at N = 100 / 400 / 2000 / 10000 (-26.7% to -8.8%). The study fixes num_samples at 200 DOCUMENTS, not tokens, so models with different tokenizer efficiency contribute different N and land at different points on that bias curve.
github_reason: Executed the installed scikit-dimension 0.3.4 TwoNN head-to-head on four uniform d-cubes at N=2000: agreement within 0.16% at every d, with BLME systematically the slightly larger of the two, consistent with its documented choice not to lower-trim. Also validated the fit against analytic Pareto(1,d) mu samples, where the estimand has a closed form.
paper_reason: Facco et al. 2017 Fig. 2 report Two-NN recovering the true dimension of uniform hypercubes with a mild downward bias at higher d and moderate N. Reproduced: 2.0488 / 2.9656 / 4.4993 / 6.9421 for d = 2 / 3 / 5 / 8 at N=2000, i.e. essentially exact through d=3 and -10% to -13% by d=8 -- and the released skdim implementation reproduces the same bias to within 0.16%, so the deviation is the estimator's, not BLME's. The paper publishes no scalar for a language model.
confounds_reason: d_model is REFUTED as a confound by direct measurement (bit-identical under zero-padding to 4096 and under ambient re-embedding of a fixed manifold). Sample size is a real confound (-26.7% at N=100 rising to -8.8% at N=10000 for a true-8 cloud), and because the config counts documents rather than tokens it is partly a tokenizer-efficiency proxy. n_layers enters only through which layers the layerwise profile reports.
defects: CODE, THE GPU FIX WAS NEVER APPLIED TO THE CPU BRANCH: intrinsic_dim.py:262-285 uses float64 + compute_mode='donot_use_mm_for_euclid_dist', and its own comment says the default float32 mm-mode form 'catastrophically cancels when r1 << ||x||, inflating TwoNN by up to +23%'. The fallback at :293-299 then does exactly that -- X.detach().float().cpu().numpy() into sklearn NearestNeighbors(algorithm='auto'), which resolves to 'brute' at d=768 and uses the x^2+y^2-2xy identity in float32. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: exact duplicate rows get r1 = 3.576e-07 at d=768 (and 4.215e-08 at d=128, 2.107e-08 at d=32) instead of 0, so 6/6 of them PASS the r1>0 filter at :224 and enter the fit with a spurious enormous mu, where the float64 branch drops them. On one 83x768 cloud with several duplicates the CPU branch read 9.349137858 against a float64 truth of 9.853619720 -- -5.1198%, with 81/83 rows disagreeing on r1.

REACHABILITY OF THE ABOVE: real duplicates DO occur -- gpt2 hidden states have 3/83 duplicate rows at layer 0 and 1/83 at layers 6 and 12 -- and the study config sets layerwise: true, so the hidden-state path is the one that runs. At that duplicate rate the 10% tail_trim in _twonn_linear_fit absorbs the spurious mu values and the CPU branch matches the float64 truth to -0.0000% on all three real layers. The failure needs a duplicate fraction above the 10% trim. The SHIPPED default (layerwise: false) reads the embedding matrix, which has 0 duplicates in 50257 gpt2 rows.
COMPARABILITY: strong sample-size bias (-26.7% at N=100), and num_samples counts documents, so token counts differ across tokenizers.
fix: Make the CPU fallback compute the same quantity as the GPU branch: replace the sklearn call at intrinsic_dim.py:293-299 with the chunked torch.cdist(..., compute_mode='donot_use_mm_for_euclid_dist') on .double() already written above it, running on device='cpu'. That removes both the float32 Gram cancellation and the spurious nonzero r1 at duplicate rows in one change, and makes the two branches genuinely identical as the comment already claims.
